key_insight: Separate Kriging surrogates for concrete crushing and instability enable reliability assessment of FRP-reinforced concrete columns when the governing failure mode switches.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports reliability estimation for slender FRP-RC columns, including rare-failure cases where direct Monte Carlo simulation detects no failures.
method: Train one Kriging model per failure mode using only FE analyses where that mode governs, then take the minimum prediction.
Use active learning, data-starvation safeguards, and post-convergence refinement guided by leave-one-out calibration and reliability-index uncertainty.
Search for surrogate design points and perform importance sampling around them.
evidence_signal: In the mixed-failure column example, reported training-point concentrations near the mode boundary were 79% and 62%; design-point and Monte Carlo reliability indices differed by at most 0.05, and FE verification at the design point agreed within 0.6%.
watch_item: Rarely governing failure modes can lack training data, making branch-specific safeguards and FE validation important.
paper_title: Reliability Assessment of FRP-RC Columns Using AK-MCS with a Piecewise Two-Branch Approach
